purpose: Test a non-PC/non-MQ global parity route: the central Alon-Tarsi coefficient of a 4-regular graph polynomial. Give an explicit 3-colourable 4-regular Hamiltonian graph for which that coefficient is zero. Thus central Eulerian-orientation parity is a strong sufficient certificate but not an exact 3-colourability decision carrier even on Hamiltonian-plus-2-factor geometry.

graph_control.regularity: Every vertex has degree four; deleting the displayed Hamiltonian cycle leaves the displayed 7-cycle.

central_coefficient.target: c_G=[product_v x_v^2] P_G(x), since |E|=2|V| for a 4-regular graph.
central_coefficient.orientation_interpretation: By the Alon-Tarsi coefficient/orientation correspondence, c_G is a signed even-minus-odd Eulerian-orientation/subgraph count for an orientation with outdegree exponent two at every vertex. Nonzero c_G is a sufficient certificate for 3-choosability and hence 3-colourability.
central_coefficient.exact_control_result: The checker enumerates all 2^14 endpoint choices in the polynomial expansion. Exactly 60 terms have exponent two at every vertex, and their signs cancel to c_G=0.

theorem.name: CENTRAL_ALON_TARSI_COEFFICIENT_IS_NOT_COMPLETE_FOR_HAMILTONIAN_4REGULAR_3COLOR
theorem.statement: There exists a 4-regular Hamiltonian 3-colourable graph with central coefficient c_G=0; the displayed seven-vertex graph is such an example.
proof: The displayed colouring is checked against all 14 edges and is proper.
The displayed Hamiltonian and complementary cycles partition the 14 edges.
theorem.scope: This refutes only completeness of this single central coefficient test. It does not rule out other monomial coefficients, other Alon-Tarsi orientations, parity systems, or polynomially searchable families of certificates.

killed: Decide 3-colourability of the Hamiltonian 4-regular source by testing only whether the central coefficient [prod x_v^2]P_G is nonzero.
Treat cancellation of the central Eulerian parity count as UNSAT/non-3-colourability evidence.
positive: Alon-Tarsi remains a valid one-sided polynomially verifiable certificate whenever a suitable nonzero coefficient/orientation is independently found.
The cycle-plus-triangles parity proof remains a genuine exceptional source theorem, but its specific parity phenomenon cannot simply be assumed complete on longer complementary cycles.
not_killed: A polynomial search over a richer family of Alon-Tarsi orientations with a completeness theorem for the source class.
A free-fermion/Pfaffian contraction for another exact invariant.
The projective ONE_NONZERO_3 / structured-MQ exact carrier from v5.4-v5.6.

next_target.name: E8_EXACT_HAMILTONIAN_TENSION_CONTRACTION_AFTER_AT_FALSE_NEGATIVE_V5_8
next_target.directive: Keep Alon-Tarsi coefficients as optional sufficient certificates, not the exact carrier. Return to the nowhere-zero GF(3) tension/projective C4 formulation and seek an exact global invariant. Any parity candidate must distinguish the explicit seven-vertex AT false negative from genuine non-3-colourable controls and must provide witness reconstruction.

sources: Alon and Tarsi, Colorings and orientations of graphs, Combinatorica 12 (1992), 125-134.
Michael Tarsi, The graph polynomial and the number of proper vertex coloring, Annales de l'Institut Fourier 49(3), 1999.
